name: Storyworld
description: Narrated illustrated stories: cast, scenes, beats, speech lines, sounds and the worker queue, with the workflows that make the stills, voice and sound takes and the audio cut.

blueprints.name: Beat
blueprints.description: One beat (unit of meaning) of a story; holds the still brief and camera move.

payload.name: Beat
payload.description: One beat (unit of meaning) of a story; holds the still brief and camera move.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Number
fields.helpText: Zero-padded beat number, 01 to 24.

fields.label: Scene (scene entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the scene this beat happens in: it brings the place, light and set dressing.

fields.label: Cast in frame (cast-member slugs)
fields.helpText: Comma-separated cast-member slugs, e.g. old-ship-cook,pirate-captain. Leave empty for a beat with no lead in frame.

fields.label: Reference pictures (asset slugs)
fields.helpText: Comma-separated asset slugs of the masters the still goes by: the cast in frame, filled from their master. A step reads it as ${entry.data.references}.

fields.label: Expression and action
fields.helpText: What each person is doing and how their face reads. A master's smile wins unless this says otherwise, so be explicit (e.g. mouth a flat line, brows level).

fields.label: Focus prop
fields.helpText: The one prop the frame is about, e.g. the onion.

fields.label: Lead-in (seconds)
fields.helpText: Quiet (or just sound effects) before the first spoken line. Empty: 0.3 s. Lengthen it to let an establishing sound breathe, e.g. waves and gulls over a picture of the ship.

fields.label: Gap between lines (seconds)
fields.helpText: Pause between two spoken lines in this beat. Empty: 0.25 s.

fields.label: Tail (seconds)
fields.helpText: Room after the last spoken line before the next beat. Empty: 0.35 s.

fields.label: Sound effects
fields.helpText: Sounds under this beat: [{"sound": "<sound slug>", "at": 0, "volume": 0.6}]. `at` is seconds from the start of the beat; volume empty uses the sound's own.

fields.label: Ambience level for this beat (0–1)
fields.helpText: Overrides the scene's level for this beat only, e.g. 0.04 when the cabin goes quiet for the letters. Empty: the scene's.

fields.label: Shot (composition from the beat sheet)
fields.helpText: The beat sheet's still / composition line, verbatim. The scene, cast and expression are added to it when the still is made.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: Set to queued to make a still for this beat: you are asked to approve the spend, see the picture, then keep it or redo (redo queues it again).

blueprints.name: Voice
blueprints.description: A speaker's ElevenLabs voice and settings.

payload.name: Voice
payload.description: A speaker's ElevenLabs voice and settings.

fields.label: Speaker
fields.helpText: Narrator, Cook, Captain, ...

blueprints.name: Still
blueprints.description: A source still: its prompt, reference pictures and generated image. Several beats can share one.

payload.name: Still
payload.description: A source still: its prompt, reference pictures and generated image. Several beats can share one.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Beats served
fields.helpText: List of beat numbers this still serves.

fields.label: References
fields.helpText: Master pictures and the style sheet.

blueprints.name: Scene
blueprints.description: A place in a story and everything always in it: the light, the set dressing and the continuity props. Every beat in the scene inherits it.

payload.name: Scene
payload.description: A place in a story and everything always in it: the light, the set dressing and the continuity props. Every beat in the scene inherits it.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry.

fields.label: Place
fields.helpText: What the place is: the structure and layout, from the approved reference photo.

fields.label: Light and time of day
fields.helpText: e.g. daylight through arched windows, warm lantern light.

fields.label: Set dressing (always there)
fields.helpText: Objects that stay on the set for every beat here. Say what is NOT there too (no extra props).

fields.label: Continuity notes
fields.helpText: What carries between beats: where the onion is, what has changed on the table.

fields.label: Ambience (sound slug)
fields.helpText: The sound that runs under every beat in this scene, e.g. the-last-onion-sound-harbour. It plays as one continuous bed, looped, and crossfades where the place changes.

fields.label: Ambience level (0–1)
fields.helpText: Loud outside (about 0.7), very low inside (about 0.1). Empty: the sound's own level.

fields.label: Heard from inside (muffled)
fields.helpText: On for an indoor scene: the same sound, low-passed as if through a wall.

fields.label: Reference photo id
fields.helpText: The source photo's id (ChatGPT library file) while it lives outside Marvin.

fields.label: Approved illustrated anchor
fields.helpText: The approved painted look of this place. Photos govern structure only.

blueprints.name: Render Job
blueprints.description: A request to the renderer for a rough cut or final video.

payload.name: Render Job
payload.description: A request to the renderer for a rough cut or final video.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Audio cut
fields.helpText: The stitched sound of the recorded lines (an audio-cut job). Play it, then say where a part needs to change.

fields.label: Timeline
fields.helpText: Where each line sits in the cut: start and end in seconds, with the speech line's slug, so a time you heard maps to the line to change.

blueprints.name: Job
blueprints.description: A heavy task handed to a worker: what to run (kind, args) and how it went. The dispatcher picks up queued jobs, starts a worker for each, and the worker writes the outcome back here.

payload.name: Job
payload.description: A heavy task handed to a worker: what to run (kind, args) and how it went. The dispatcher picks up queued jobs, starts a worker for each, and the worker writes the outcome back here.

fields.label: Kind
fields.helpText: What to run: a kind of job the worker image has (see Job kinds), e.g. audio-cut.

fields.label: Arguments
fields.helpText: The job's own input, e.g. {"story": "the-last-onion"}.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: queued: waiting for the dispatcher. claimed: picked up and being started. running: the worker is on it. done or failed.

fields.label: Result
fields.helpText: What the job produced: asset ids, a timeline, counts.

fields.label: Log
fields.helpText: What happened, and why it failed if it did.

fields.label: Claimed at
fields.helpText: When the dispatcher picked it up (UTC, ISO). A claimed or running job with no progress past its kind's timeout is marked failed.

fields.label: Claimed by
fields.helpText: Which worker took it.

blueprints.name: Job kind
blueprints.description: A kind of job and where it runs: which image does it, how it is started, and how long it may take.

payload.name: Job kind
payload.description: A kind of job and where it runs: which image does it, how it is started, and how long it may take.

fields.label: Kind
fields.helpText: The name jobs ask for, e.g. audio-cut.

fields.label: How it is started
fields.helpText: kubernetes: a Job per run. docker: a container per run on a Docker host. http: sent to a standing worker's URL. local: a process on the dispatcher's own machine.

fields.label: Image
fields.helpText: The container image that does this kind (kubernetes and docker modes).

fields.label: Worker URL
fields.helpText: http mode: the standing worker's address (its /jobs).

fields.label: Resources
fields.helpText: Kubernetes requests and limits, e.g. {"cpu": "1", "memory": "1Gi"}.

blueprints.name: Sound
blueprints.description: A reusable sound for any story: what it sounds like and its take. Beats place sounds under their picture; scenes use one as an ambience. Tag it so it can be found again (spoon, kitchen, ambience).

payload.name: Sound
payload.description: A reusable sound for any story: what it sounds like and its take. Beats place sounds under their picture; scenes use one as an ambience. Tag it so it can be found again (spoon, kitchen, ambience).

fields.label: Made for (story slug, optional)
fields.helpText: Where it was first used. A sound belongs to the library, not to a story: any story can use it by naming its slug.

fields.label: What it sounds like
fields.helpText: Describe it plainly: 'gentle waves lapping a wooden ship hull, a few distant seagulls, rigging creaking'.

fields.label: Kind
fields.helpText: effect: a moment (a spoon on a bowl). ambience: a bed that runs under a scene (waves and gulls).

fields.label: Where the take came from
fields.helpText: generated: made from the description. uploaded or recorded: your own file, attached as the take.

fields.label: Length (0.5–30 s)
fields.helpText: Empty: ElevenLabs picks from the description.

fields.label: Loop smoothly
fields.helpText: On for ambience that has to run under a longer beat.

fields.label: Volume (0–1)
fields.helpText: Level under the narration; a beat can override it.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: Set to queued to make a new take: you are asked to approve the spend, hear the take, then keep it or redo (redo queues it again).

blueprints.name: Worker
blueprints.description: A dispatcher's heartbeat: it rewrites last_seen about once a minute, so Settings → Workers can show whether anything is watching the queue.

payload.name: Worker
payload.description: A dispatcher's heartbeat: it rewrites last_seen about once a minute, so Settings → Workers can show whether anything is watching the queue.

fields.label: Role
fields.helpText: dispatcher

fields.label: Starts
fields.helpText: The modes it starts workers in, e.g. docker, kubernetes.

fields.label: Last seen
fields.helpText: UTC, ISO. Written by the dispatcher about once a minute.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: idle or busy.

fields.label: Current job
fields.helpText: The job it is running now, if any.

fields.label: Kinds it can do
fields.helpText: Each kind it offers, with its contract: what it takes (inputs), the media types it accepts, what it produces, and what it needs.

fields.label: Needs / has
fields.helpText: What this machine has that its kinds need, e.g. ffmpeg.

blueprints.name: Cast Member
blueprints.description: A recurring Storyworld character: who they are and their approved master picture.

payload.name: Cast Member
payload.description: A recurring Storyworld character: who they are and their approved master picture.

fields.label: Cast id
fields.helpText: Stable id, e.g. old-ship-cook.

fields.label: Profile
fields.helpText: The cast/*.json body.

blueprints.name: Speech Line
blueprints.description: One spoken line of narration or dialogue, with its recorded audio.

payload.name: Speech Line
payload.description: One spoken line of narration or dialogue, with its recorded audio.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Text (what is spoken)
fields.helpText: The words the voice says. Fix wording, punctuation or a respelling here, then record again; this is the source of truth, the story script is a readable copy.

fields.label: Direction
fields.helpText: How this line should sound and feel, in your own words ("tired, a little amused, almost to herself"). Read by people and by Claude when choosing the voice settings and the delivery tags; the voice itself cannot read it.

fields.label: Delivery text
fields.helpText: Optional: the same words with ElevenLabs v3 tags, like [sighs] or [whispers] or [pause]. When filled in, the next take speaks this (on the v3 model) instead of Text. Captions always use Text, never this.

fields.label: On-screen caption (if different)
fields.helpText: What the caption shows when it should differ from what is spoken. Empty: the caption is the text.

fields.label: Stability (0–1)
fields.helpText: Lower is more expressive, higher more even. Empty: the voice's own setting.

fields.label: Similarity boost (0–1)
fields.helpText: Empty: the voice's own setting.

fields.label: Style (0–1)
fields.helpText: More style is more exaggerated delivery. Empty: the voice's own setting.

fields.label: Speed
fields.helpText: 1 is normal; 0.7–1.2 is the usable range. Slow a line down to give it room.

fields.label: Notes on this take
fields.helpText: What sounded strange and what you changed, so the next take is deliberate.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: Set to queued to make a new take: you are asked to approve the spend, hear the take, then keep it or redo (redo queues it again).

actions.message: Record the next ${steps.lines.output.count} spoken lines of “${entry.title}” with ElevenLabs? It uses speech credit (the whole story is about 1,300 characters). You will hear them stitched together afterwards and can fix any line.
Make the still for beat 03 (the cook at the near-empty shelf) with the cook master as the reference? It uses OpenAI image credit.

args.prompt: Use the reference picture for the old ship cook: keep his face shape, hair, beard, build, clothes, peg leg and the rounded miniature illustration style exactly as drawn. New scene: the cook stands in front of an almost empty wooden provision shelf in a ship's hold, warm lantern light. Only three things sit on the otherwise bare shelf, clearly visible together: two small scraps of pork, one flat hard ship's biscuit with a few small weevil holes in it, and a single onion. His brows are tilted down and his mouth is a flat, tired line: weary resignation, not a smile. Vertical portrait composition, the same warm palette and soft rounded shapes. No text, no writing.

actions.message: Redo beat 04 (cook and captain, cabin two-shot) with the unfinished letters on the table and no invented props? It uses OpenAI image credit.

args.prompt: Two reference pictures: the old ship cook (peg leg, apron) and the pirate captain (navy and gold coat, burgundy waistcoat, auburn hair). Keep each character's face, hair, build, clothes and the rounded miniature illustration style exactly as drawn in their reference. New scene: the captain's cabin, warm lantern light, a plain wooden table. The captain sits behind a spread nautical chart, composed and dismissive. A single whole onion lies in the middle of the chart. The cook stands at the table's edge, his hand just withdrawn from the onion, chin slightly lifted. His mouth is a flat straight line and his brows are level: deadpan, not smiling. On the table beside the chart: a few folded letters, an inkwell with a quill, and one open unfinished sheet near the captain's hand with only faint scribbled lines, no readable writing. Both characters clearly visible together, a cabin two-shot. Keep the cabin simple: no sextant, globe, painting or other extra props. Vertical portrait composition, the same warm palette and soft rounded shapes. No text, no letters, no writing.

actions.message: Keep this still for beat 04? Check both faces against their masters.
Record ${entry.data.speaker}: “${entry.data.text}” with ElevenLabs? It uses speech credit (${entry.data.text|length} characters).

data.take_notes: Recorded as written. Listen, then Keep or Redo. Every take stays attached to this line as a take; Audio uses the one set here.

actions.message: Listen to this take of ${entry.data.speaker}: “${entry.data.text}” (${steps.say.output.asset.duration_seconds} s). Redo records a fresh take and asks again; change the wording or the voice settings on the line first if it should sound different.
